statements.t: We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering the discovery and development of a new class of RNA-targeting therapeutics with the goal of upregulating gene expression and restoring healthy protein levels to treat a broad range of genetic diseases.
While we believe that it remains underdiagnosed, we estimate that there are approximately 21,000 individuals living with SYNGAP1 in the United States and the five largest European markets.
We expect to dose the first patient in the ASCEND Phase 1/2 clinical trial in the fourth quarter of 2026.

In addition to our SYNGAP1 program, we are advancing a preclinical program targeting SHANK3 for Phelan-McDermid syndrome, a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by autism, developmental delay, intellectual disability, motor impairment and milestone regression, for which there are no approved disease-modifying treatments.
We estimate that there are more than 45,000 patients with Phelan-McDermid syndrome in the United States.
We expect to designate a development candidate in the SHANK3 program in 2027.

Additionally, we intend to leverage strategic discovery partnerships, including our research, collaboration, and license agreement with GlaxoSmithKline Intellectual Property (No.3) Limited ("GSK"), to extend the application of our RAP Platform beyond the CNS and validate our approach to gene upregulation in additional tissues and disease areas.
Once a disease-associated target gene is identified, we apply our RAP Platform to identify the controlling regRNA and rapidly generate novel ASO candidates.

If we obtain regulatory approval for our product candidates, we expect to incur significant expenses related to developing our commercialization capability to support product sales, marketing and distribution.
We anticipate that our expenses will increase substantially if and as we:

Because of the numerous risks and uncertainties associated with the development of therapeutics, we are unable to accurately predict the timing or amount of increased expenses and when, or if, we will be able to achieve or maintain profitability.

We will not generate revenue from product sales unless and until we successfully complete clinical development and obtain regulatory approval for our current or any future product candidates, which we expect will take a number of years or may never occur.
As a result, we will need substantial additional funding to support our continuing operations and pursue our growth strategy.

Until such time as we can generate significant revenue from product sales, if ever, we expect to finance our operations through equity offerings, debt financings, or other capital sources, including current and potential future collaborations, license agreements, and other similar arrangements.

If we fail to raise capital or enter into such agreements or arrangements as, and when needed, we may delay, limit, reduce or terminate our product development or future commercialization efforts or grant rights to develop and market product candidates that we would otherwise develop and market ourselves, or even cease operations.
However, we have based this estimate on assumptions that may prove to be wrong, and we could deplete our capital resources sooner than we currently expect.
We do not own or operate and currently have no plans to establish any manufacturing facilities.
We rely, and expect to continue to rely, on third parties for preclinical and clinical supply as well as commercial supply if we obtain marketing approval.

In addition, we rely on third parties to package, label, store, and distribute our clinical supply and we intend to rely on third parties to conduct the same activities for our commercial products if we obtain regulatory approval.
We expect to incur significant expenses and operating losses in the foreseeable future as we advance the development of product candidates.
Pursuant to the Sales Agreement, we will pay the sales agent a commission rate of up to 3.0% of the gross proceeds from the sale of any shares of our common stock.
There is no assurance that we will succeed in obtaining sufficient funding on terms acceptable to us to fund continuing operations, if at all.

We expect our expenses to increase substantially in connection with our ongoing activities, particularly as we continue our development of, seek regulatory approval for, and potentially commercialize our product candidates and seek to discover and develop additional product candidates, conduct our ongoing and planned clinical trials and preclinical studies, continue our R&D activities, hire additional personnel,…

Until such time, if ever, we can generate substantial product revenues, we expect to finance our operations through the sale of equity securities, debt financings, working capital lines of credit, strategic alliances and/or license arrangements, grant funding, interest income earned on invested cash balances or a combination of two or more of these sources.

To the extent we raise additional capital through the sale of equity or convertible debt securities, investors’ ownership interest will be diluted, and the terms of these securities may include liquidation or other preferences that adversely affect the rights of a common stockholder.

estimates.t: There have been no significant changes to our critical accounting estimates in the preparation of our condensed consolidated financial statements during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to those disclosed in our 2025 Form 10-K.
